summary: This document updates RFC 7001 by creating a registry for property types in the Authentication-Results email header field, rather than limiting use to the original small set. It was replaced by RFC 7601.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7410 allows the Authentication-Results email header to use additional property types. It creates an IANA registry for those types and says consumers ignore results with a type they do not understand.

questions: what are ptype values in authentication-results
how are new authentication property types registered
what should software do with an unknown ptype
subtitle: A registry for property types in the Authentication-Results email header.

tldr.problem: The Authentication-Results header had a small fixed set of property types, while users wanted to report other kinds of properties.
tldr.mechanism: IANA creates an Email Authentication Property Types registry with Expert Review for new entries.
tldr.outcome: RFC 7410 updates RFC 7001 and was obsoleted by RFC 7601.

today: RFC 7410 was obsoleted by RFC 7601 and updates RFC 7001, according to the unit metadata.

sections.title: Authentication Results and Ptypes
sections.content: RFC 7001 defines the Authentication-Results header field to present authentication results in a machine-readable form. It originally listed a small set of property types, or ptypes. RFC 7410 updates that definition to allow additional ptypes and creates a registry for recording them and their defining documents.
sections.plainLanguage: The header reports authentication results for software to read. This RFC lets it describe more kinds of properties than the original set.

sections.title: The Property Type Registry
sections.content: IANA created the Email Authentication Property Types subregistry within Email Authentication Parameters. Each entry includes a ptype token and a short description; a reference to a defining document is optional. Initial values are body, header, policy, and smtp. New entries are subject to Expert Review.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry lists each property type and what it describes. An expert reviews new entries before they are added.

sections.title: Handling Unknown Types
sections.content: The RFC notes that older software may not know a new ptype. A consumer can reject a message or ignore the part of the result using that type; the RFC generally advises ignoring unknown ptypes. A consumer that does not understand a ptype ignores the result reported with it.
sections.plainLanguage: Older software may encounter a type it does not know. The RFC generally advises it to ignore that result and continue processing.
